samples.question: I make music. Help me shape a digital product.

response.answer:
My first bet: a small pack of original, edit-ready loops for independent video editors. Sell the time they save clearing and cutting music. Include stems, tempo, a usage license and a short demo cut.

Send a private demo to three editors who regularly license music. Ask them to use one loop in an actual cut, then offer the full pack at a stated price. A paid order is a stronger signal than a compliment.

Which editors can you reach, and which style of music do you already own the rights to?

samples.question: What do I keep on a €1,500 service that costs €900 to deliver?

response.answer:
You keep €600 per sale before fixed costs and tax. That’s a 40% contribution margin.

€1,500 price − €900 variable cost = €600 contribution.

This uses your stated assumptions. Check whether delivery cost includes review time, payment fees and refunds before committing to the price.

samples.question: What should I charge to keep a 40% margin? (third turn)

response.answer:
Charge at least €1,833.34 per sale to keep a 40% contribution margin at €1,100 in variable cost. That leaves €733.34 before fixed costs and tax.

Price floor = €1,100 ÷ (1 − 40%), rounded up to the next cent when needed.

That is your financial floor. Test whether a buyer will pay it. Recalculate any price-dependent processing fees at the new price.

artifact.markdown:
# Minimum offer price

Charge at least €1,833.34 per sale to keep a 40% contribution margin at €1,100 in variable cost. That leaves €733.34 before fixed costs and tax.

Price floor = €1,100 ÷ (1 − 40%), rounded up to the next cent when needed.

That is your financial floor. Test whether a buyer will pay it. Recalculate any price-dependent processing fees at the new price.

Basis: Unit contribution before fixed costs and tax. Cost is assumed constant over the prices considered. This is not evidence of buyer demand.
